long_biography.plain_text:
Lint worked as an aerospace designer, tugboat captain and international vessel-delivery captain, beginning his maritime career in early adulthood. He captained working vessels in the Pacific Northwest and participated in the Exxon Valdez cleanup. Over time, his engineering background and practical seamanship drew him toward historic boats that commercial operators had abandoned.

In 2010 he took responsibility for a nineteenth-century steel vessel that had spent a decade out of service. Lint returned her to operation, oversaw repeated hull repairs and hoped to establish a floating museum. He also revived the fire-damaged ferry Kirkland and cared for the classic vessel Northwind. His work ranged from emergency repairs and salvage to long-distance delivery, restoration and public maritime education.

Both establish the year and deceased status, but the month and day are left unproposed because the wording does not resolve whether death occurred immediately or after the collision.
